tr: „Don't move him! That is a danger.“
en: „Don't move him! That is a danger.“

tr: „And I'll send you a message every day!“
en: „And I'll send you a message every day!“

tr: „A man is on the ground. He doesn't move.“
en: „A man is on the ground. He doesn't move.“

tr: „No, I didn't finish it. I do it tonight.“
en: „No, I didn't finish it. I do it tonight.“

tr: „July is good. I'll write you the address.“
en: „July is good. I'll write you the address.“

tr: Diş hekiminde. Ne zaman ağrıyor, sebebi ne?
en: At the dentist's. When does it hurt, and what is the cause?

tr: „No, I didn't finish. I have two hours today.“
en: „No, I didn't finish. I have two hours today.“

tr: Postanede mektup ve paket. Hangi fiyat neye ait?
en: A letter and a parcel at the post office. Which price belongs to what?

tr: „You shouldn't smoke.“ — en kısa öğüt, tek fiille.
en: „You shouldn't smoke.“ — the shortest advice, with a single verb.

tr: Sağlıklı yaşam öğütleri. Ne yapmalı, ne yapmamalı?
en: Advice for healthy living. What should you do, what should you not?

tr: A1'in son yazma egzersizi: düzensiz geçmiş ve veda.
en: The last writing task of A1: the irregular past and a farewell.

tr: Önce mektup, sonra pul, sonra paket, en son toplam.
en: First the letter, then the stamp, then the parcel, last the total.

tr: Önce genel soru, sonra iş, sonra yer, en son ulaşım.
en: First the general question, then the work, then the place, last the transport.

tr: „Sorry, I can't hear you. Can you speak more slowly?“
en: „Sorry, I can't hear you. Can you speak more slowly?“

tr: İnternet ve uygulama konuşuluyor. Parola neden sorun?
en: The internet and an app are the subject. Why is the password a problem?

tr: Önce soru, sonra şikâyet, sonra ayrıntı, en son tedavi.
en: First the question, then the complaint, then the detail, last the treatment.

tr: „My password doesn't work too.“ — yeni bir tane istiyor.
en: „My password doesn't work too.“ — he asks for a new one.

tr: E-posta kalıplarını yaz. Sonunda e-posta formunu doldur.
en: Write the phrases of an email. At the end, fill in the email form.

tr: Önce bağlantı, sonra haber, sonra öğüt, en son yeni gün.
en: First getting through, then the news, then the advice, last the new day.

tr: „Then it is two euros.“ — bir euro pul, dokuz euro paket.
en: „Then it is two euros.“ — one euro is the stamp, nine the parcel.

tr: Geçmişte „olmak“ fiili. „was“ ve „were“ art arda geçiyor.
en: The verb „be“ in the past. „was“ and „were“ come one after the other.

tr: Önce ayrılık, sonra söz, sonra davet, en son kesin tarih.
en: First the parting, then the promise, then the invitation, last the fixed date.

tr: Acil bir durum. Emirler art arda geliyor — kim ne yapıyor?
en: An emergency. The orders come one after the other — who does what?

tr: Kısa bir e-posta. Soru ne, sorun ne, geçen hafta ne olmuş?
en: A short email. What is the question, what the problem, what was last week?

tr: „Then let's meet again in July.“ — yaz genel, temmuz kesin.
en: „Then let's meet again in July.“ — the summer is vague, July is fixed.

tr: „You should sleep eight hours.“ — beş ve altı şu anki hâli.
en: „You should sleep eight hours.“ — five and six is how it is now.

tr: Önce davet, sonra ret, sonra erteleme, en son buluşma yeri.
en: First the invitation, then the refusal, then the delay, last the meeting place.

tr: „Yesterday I was at home all day.“ — İrlanda geçen haftaydı.
en: „Yesterday I was at home all day.“ — Ireland was last week.

tr: Eczanede ilaç alınıyor. Günde kaç kez, ne kadar, kime uygun?
en: Medicine is bought at the chemist's. How many times a day, how much, and for whom?

tr: „…but the people were friendly.“ — çoğul özne „were“ istiyor.
en: „…but the people were friendly.“ — a plural subject takes „were“.

tr: „Call me tomorrow and tell me.“ — gelmeyecek, yalnız arayacak.
en: „Call me tomorrow and tell me.“ — he is not coming, he is only calling.

tr: „I use the internet for my class.“ — video kız kardeşinin işi.
en: „I use the internet for my class.“ — the video is her sister's doing.

tr: Eczane ve rapor cümlelerini yaz. Sonunda eczane fişini doldur.
en: Write sentences for the chemist's and for calling in sick. At the end, fill in the chemist's slip.

tr: Öğüt ve acil çağrı yaz. „should“ kural değil tavsiye söylüyor.
en: Write advice and an emergency call. „should“ states no rule, only advice.

tr: „You should sleep more.“ — „should“ sonrası fiil eksiz kalıyor.
en: „You should sleep more.“ — after „should“ the verb stays bare.

tr: Geçmiş zamanı yaz. Olumsuzda ve soruda fiil ilk hâline dönüyor.
en: Write the past. In the negative and in questions the verb goes back to its base form.

tr: İşe rapor bildiriliyor. Bugün ne oluyor, yarın ne, öbür gün ne?
en: Calling in sick at work. What happens today, what tomorrow, what the day after?

tr: Önce yardım çağrısı, sonra ambulans, sonra uyarı, en son ceket.
en: First the call for help, then the ambulance, then the warning, last the jacket.

tr: „I'm not feeling well. I can't come to work today.“ — ilacı var.
en: „I'm not feeling well. I can't come to work today.“ — he does have medicine.

tr: İki kişi hafta sonunu anlatıyor. Kim nereye gitti, kim ne yaptı?
en: Two people talk about the weekend. Who went where, who did what?

tr: Mesajlaşma anlatılıyor. Hangi durumda mesaj, hangisinde telefon?
en: Texting is the subject. When a message, and when a call?

tr: „But I'll call you every week.“ — her gün mesaj atacak olan Kaan.
en: „But I'll call you every week.“ — the one texting every day is Kaan.

tr: A1'in son metni: bir veda. Sonra ne olacak, ne zaman görüşülecek?
en: The last text of A1: a farewell. What comes next, and when do they meet?

tr: Geçen hafta sonu anlatılıyor. Düzensiz geçmiş biçimlerini yakala.
en: Last weekend is told. Catch the irregular past forms.

tr: „But for bad news I always call.“ — kötü haber mesajla verilmiyor.
en: „But for bad news I always call.“ — bad news is not given by message.

tr: Geçmişte soru sorma. Dikkat: „did“ varken fiil ilk hâline dönüyor.
en: Asking questions in the past. Careful: with „did“ the verb goes back to its base form.

tr: „I went to the mountains with two friends.“ — büyükanne pazar günü.
en: „I went to the mountains with two friends.“ — the grandmother comes on Sunday.

tr: „Twenty minutes a day is good.“ — üç, yürüme koşma yüzmenin sayısı.
en: „Twenty minutes a day is good.“ — three is the number of walking, running and swimming.

tr: „Yes, full. Books and a plastic box.“ — kâğıt ve fotoğraf mektupta.
en: „Yes, full. Books and a plastic box.“ — the paper and the photo are in the letter.

tr: Bir arkadaş öğüt veriyor. „should“ ve „shouldn't“ art arda geliyor.
en: A friend gives advice. „should“ and „shouldn't“ come one after the other.

tr: Diş ağrısını iki biçimde de yaz. Sonunda diş hekimi formunu doldur.
en: Write the toothache in both ways. At the end, fill in the dentist's form.

tr: „Then you shouldn't drink coffee after six! Try water or light tea.“
en: „Then you shouldn't drink coffee after six! Try water or light tea.“

tr: „Good. Twelve euros together, please.“ — iki artı dokuz artı iki pul.
en: „Good. Twelve euros together, please.“ — two plus nine plus two stamps.

tr: Geçmişte „olmak“ fiilini yaz. Tek fiilin iki biçimi var: was ve were.
en: Write „be“ in the past. One verb, two forms: was and were.

tr: „Can you send me a new one?“ — „one“ burada „password“ yerine geçiyor.
en: „Can you send me a new one?“ — „one“ stands for „password“ here.

tr: „I didn't win, but it was good.“ — „didn't“ sonrası „win“ ilk hâlinde.
en: „I didn't win, but it was good.“ — after „didn't“, „win“ is in its base form.

tr: „I know. I am here after four years.“ — her yıl gelmek öğüdün kendisi.
en: „I know. I am here after four years.“ — coming every year is the advice itself.

tr: „I went to a farm near the mountains.“ — anne babayı ziyaret eden Nil.
en: „I went to a farm near the mountains.“ — the one visiting her parents is Nil.

tr: Telefon cümlelerini yaz. Telefonda kendini „this is“ ile tanıtıyorsun.
en: Write sentences for the phone. On the phone you introduce yourself with „this is“.

tr: „Can I speak to Mr. Demir, please?“ — „speak to“ birine konuşmak demek.
en: „Can I speak to Mr. Demir, please?“ — „speak to“ means to talk to somebody.

tr: „Don't come tomorrow. Come on Thursday.“ — yarın yalnız telefon edecek.
en: „Don't come tomorrow. Come on Thursday.“ — tomorrow he only calls.

tr: „On Sunday I visited my grandmother.“ — düzenli geçmiş: visit → visited.
en: „On Sunday I visited my grandmother.“ — the regular past: visit → visited.

tr: „The app is the same website, only smaller.“ — daha küçük ama aynı site.
en: „The app is the same website, only smaller.“ — smaller, but the same site.

tr: „The weather was cold but the people were friendly.“ — güneşli olan göl.
en: „The weather was cold but the people were friendly.“ — the sunny place was the lake.

tr: „Where did you go last weekend?“ — „did“ varken fiil „go“, „went“ değil.
en: „Where did you go last weekend?“ — with „did“ the verb is „go“, not „went“.

tr: Telefonda kendini tanıtma. Dikkat: yüz yüze „I am“, telefonda „this is“.
en: Introducing yourself on the phone. Careful: face to face „I am“, on the phone „this is“.

tr: Önce dün, sonra geçen hafta, sonra o haftanın akşamı, en son arkadaşları.
en: First yesterday, then last week, then the evening of that week, last his friends.

tr: „I use the internet for my class.“ — „the internet“ hep „the“ ile geliyor.
en: „I use the internet for my class.“ — „the internet“ always comes with „the“.

tr: „I have a toothache. My tooth hurts since two days.“ — aynı şey iki kalıpla.
en: „I have a toothache. My tooth hurts since two days.“ — the same thing with two patterns.

tr: „I have a headache. Can I have some medicine, please?“ — su ilacı içmek için.
en: „I have a headache. Can I have some medicine, please?“ — the water is for taking it.

tr: „Good! At seven, in the café next to the park.“ — iki saat, cevabın gecikmesi.
en: „Good! At seven, in the café next to the park.“ — two hours is how late the reply came.

tr: „I eat a big dinner at ten in the evening.“ — hafif akşam yemeği öğüdün kendisi.
en: „I eat a big dinner at ten in the evening.“ — the light dinner is the advice itself.

tr: „Three times: morning, afternoon and evening.“ — bir tanedir her seferde, altı fiyat.
en: „Three times: morning, afternoon and evening.“ — one each time, six is the price.

tr: „I didn't watch TV in the evening — I was too tired.“ — „didn't“ sonrası fiil ilk hâlinde.
en: „I didn't watch TV in the evening — I was too tired.“ — after „didn't“ the verb is in its base form.
